question: Does the corrected opt-in strict whole-solve work cap preserve historically observed winners from early, repair, and admissible-order phases while enforcing the declared work ceiling?
nonDuplication: ETT-019 established cap enforcement on a success-censored affected cohort but could not test solve safety. This cold targeted cohort deliberately includes three historical admissible-order winners, three earlier main-ladder controls, and two repair winners; it is not another admissible-reserve treatment.

sampleSelection.rule: fixed historical phase-balanced diagnostic: all three known admissible-order winners in prior campaign slices plus three main-ladder and two repair-probe winners under the same 300k-node/400k-work nominal resources; no replacements
sampleSelection.policyInput: mechanics-only worker input; historical outcomes select the diagnostic sample but are not supplied to the solver

primaryOutcome: paired solved set with symmetric strict gains and losses
stoppingRule: run the fixed eight rows once per arm; no replacements or extension
escalationRule: only nominate a separate held-out population experiment if strict retains all 8/8 historical winners and remains within the pre-existing 4096-work checkpoint tolerance on 8/8
productionDecision: no promotion from this intentionally outcome-selected targeted diagnostic
protocolAudit: The frozen protocol used JSON-array hashing instead of the campaign validator newline convention. The level IDs/order were unchanged; the hash field was corrected after execution. This is an additional reason the run is not preregistered or decision-bearing. Arm roles/artifact names were also added post-run after the analyzer exposed that historical list ordering inverted treatment labels; arm contents and treatment were unambiguous in commands and artifacts.
